references.text: The introduction to the Nazirite law describing the vow of consecration to the Lord, which verse 13 addresses as its conclusion.
Describes the period of the Nazirite vow and that the hair must not be cut until the days are completed, a point referred to in verse 13.
Continuation of the ritual at the entrance of the tabernacle where the Nazirite shaves their consecrated head.
An offering shall be brought at the entrance of the tent of meeting, the same place where the Nazirite is to come.
The entrance of the tent of meeting as the place for bringing an offering before the Lord's presence.
Samson was consecrated as a Nazirite from his mother's womb, an example of the Nazirite vow in practice.
Paul participates in the purification ritual with men who had taken a vow, a continuation of Nazirite practice in the New Testament.
Paul cut his hair at Cenchreae because he had taken a vow, likely a Nazirite vow.
